why: THE FACTORY'S OWN HEARTBEAT, and until 2026-09-12 nothing had one. The pulse belt is universal state - one file, at the factory root, written by the one machine that owns it - and the machine has been built, gated and in CI since `The pulse is universal state, not repo state (#2)`. It had never executed. Not once. `.refer-factory/pulse-belt.jsonl` did not exist, because this repo declared eighteen machines and zero triggers, so universal state had nothing universal writing it. Operator, 2026-09-12: 'why i'm not seeing the pulse on the belt on incoming and resolved' - the answer was that there was no belt, and the reason the question was hard to chase is that `npm run gate:pulse-belt` passes honestly against throwaway fixtures. The machine works. Nothing ran it. A machine nothing declares is invisible rather than broken, which is the failure shape `triggers.cjs` names in its own header as the one this factory exists to remove. DECLARED HERE, BESIDE THIS REPO'S OWN MACHINERY, AND NOT IN machines/ - that directory is one copy for every repo, so a trigger in it would ship this repo's cadence to all of them. The machine is universal, the cadence is local; this file is the local half. EVERY MUST STAY 5m, and this is the trap. pulse-belt.cjs line 208 breaks out of its search the moment it finds a trigger whose id is `pulse-belt` - 'our own declaration wins over the tick's' - so this `every` sets the STAGE LENGTH, not merely how often the machine is invoked. Run it every 15m while declaring 5m and the board draws a cycle that disagrees with the clock that made it, which the machine's own header calls a display that lies. It is also exactly the collision that forced the `pulse` -> `pulse-check` rename on the same day: two different things wearing one name, on two different clocks. Three stages at 5m means a card is visible for 15 minutes total - incoming, then belt, then resolved - so a single run only ever shows beat 1 with belt and resolved empty, and that is correct rather than broken. DRIVEN BY THE CLAUDE ROUTINE `living-factory-pulse`, rooted in this folder since 2026-09-13, which runs `npm run pulse` every five minutes and nothing else. `drivenBy` rather than `run` is deliberate and follows `pulse.trigger.json`: an external clock drives this, so no scheduler may ever fire it as well. It is a routine rather than an engine or an OS task for three reasons, each learned the expensive way. The engine cannot be pointed here: `schedule.cjs` line 86 is `path.resolve(__dirname, '../..')`, so it always drives the repo it lives in. The operator ruled out OS-level tasks, because the Claude routine already existed. And a routine only reaches its own working folder without a permission prompt: on 2026-09-12 this pulse was added as a second command to that routine while it was rooted in Telechurch, the command crossed into this folder, and the run hung on a prompt nobody could answer. So the routine was moved here and given one command. The pulse doctrine still holds: 'deliberately the stupidest component in the factory: one tool, no judgement, nothing that can prompt'. Until the routine actually ticks, this declaration still does work: it is what lets the machine say GAP - 'the cycle is not being driven on time' - instead of reporting beat 1 as though beat 1 were healthy.
